summary: Dedicated customer throughput drop under bursty concurrency (scheduler fairness + batching interaction)
description:
Issue summary
Northbridge Support reports a sustained throughput drop (requests/sec and tokens/sec) on their Dedicated cluster during bursty traffic. The issue reproduces when concurrency ramps quickly (bursts) and appears correlated with increased scheduler queue wait and suboptimal batch composition during the prefill/decode transition.

Customer impact
- Customer tier: Dedicated
- Impact: ~25–35% lower sustained throughput during bursts vs their prior week baseline; increased time-to-drain after burst; intermittent client-side timeouts when queue time spikes.
- Customer-visible symptoms: backlog growth during bursts; perceived “slowdown” even after burst subsides.

Environment
- Dedicated cluster: us-east
- Model(s): rw-chat-70b (primary), rw-chat-34b (fallback)
- Mode: streaming chat, mixed prompt lengths
- Recent changes: runtime upgrade in the last 7 days (exact build stamp pulled in investigation notes)

Reproduction (customer-provided + Redwood replay)
1) Generate burst: ramp concurrency from ~30 -> 220 over 20–30 seconds, hold 2–3 minutes, then drop to ~50.
2) Prompt mix: ~60% short (200–600 toks), ~30% medium (1.5k–3k toks), ~10% long (6k–10k toks). Outputs typically 150–400 toks streamed.
3) Observe tokens/sec and queue wait metrics; compare to a steady-state control run at concurrency ~120.

Initial observations (Support)
- During ramp: p95 queue wait increases sharply; batch sizes oscillate; decode utilization drops while prefill utilization spikes.
- After ramp: cluster takes longer than expected to recover (time-to-drain). Throughput remains depressed for several minutes.

Hypothesis
Scheduler fairness + batching heuristics under bursty, mixed prompt-length traffic causes batch fragmentation and increased context switching between prefill-heavy and decode-heavy work. This reduces effective GPU utilization and lowers tokens/sec, even when capacity is available.

References
- Slack thread: #eng-runtime discussion on bursty throughput + fairness tradeoffs (see internal Slack link in comments)
- Perf baseline suite: traffic shape aligns with BURSTY_CONCURRENCY ramp scenarios used in Q1 2026 baselines

Data requested from customer
- Client-side timestamps for request start, first token, completion
- Their load generator parameters (ramp rate, max inflight)
- Confirmation of whether they pin model version or allow fallback

Workaround (temporary)
- Reduce ramp slope (increase ramp duration) and/or cap max inflight during peak bursts until scheduler tuning rolls out.
- If acceptable, pin to rw-chat-34b during peak bursts to avoid long-prefill domination (customer evaluating).
comments: 2026-02-12 09:18 (Aisha Bello): Created ticket from Support escalation. Customer reports tokens/sec drop under bursty concurrency only (steady load looks normal). Assigning to Scheduling for triage. Customer is Dedicated us-east; impact ongoing during their weekday peak windows.

2026-02-12 10:02 (Sofia Ivanova): Triage: likely scheduler fairness + batching interplay. Requesting scheduler metrics from their dedicated cluster: queue_wait_ms histograms, batch_composition (prefill vs decode), backpressure counters, and effective batch size over time. Looping in Julian Moore for instrumentation sanity + load-shedding hooks.

2026-02-12 10:25 (Julian Moore): Pulled metrics from dedicated cluster (last 24h). During burst window, decode batches are frequently <4 sequences while prefill batches spike; queue depth grows despite available GPU headroom. This pattern matches what we saw in #eng-runtime variance thread. Internal link: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/eng-runtime (thread timestamp ~1706123456).

2026-02-12 11:40 (Sofia Ivanova): Reproduced in lab using benchmark harness with a bursty concurrency ramp + mixed prompt lengths. Under current batching defaults, fairness policy over-rotates to admitting new prefills during burst, starving decode and fragmenting batches. Result: ~28% drop in tokens/sec and longer drain time. Attaching run ID: benchlab-run-2026-02-12T19:32Z (see perf-canary artifacts).

2026-02-13 08:10 (Sana Farid): From variance perspective, this is outside expected noise. The delta is consistent across 5 trials in us-east on the same hardware SKU with pinned driver/CUDA. This should qualify as a regression for bursty shapes if recent runtime change adjusted fairness weights. Suggest comparing against baseline suite traffic shape and checking if any batching heuristic change landed.

2026-02-13 09:05 (Sofia Ivanova): Root cause narrowed: fairness tweak interacts badly with mixed prompt-length admission under burst. Queue wait increases because decode tokens are delayed; streaming workloads amplify perception. Proposed fix: cap prefill admission when decode queue is non-empty + adjust max batching wait under burst to stabilize batch size. Will ship behind a scheduler flag for Dedicated first.

2026-02-14 13:22 (Sofia Ivanova): Fix implemented and queued for canary on customer dedicated cluster. Related PRs: sources/github/redwood/pr-23981.json (tail cap + fairness tweak), sources/github/redwood/pr-24033.json (batching heuristic adjustment).

2026-02-17 16:50 (Aisha Bello): Canary results (2h during customer peak replay): tokens/sec recovered +31% vs pre-fix; queue_wait p95 down ~45%; time-to-drain improved. No increase in error rates observed. Proceeding to full rollout in us-east dedicated pool for this customer.

2026-02-18 12:30 (Customer via Support): Confirming improvement during our lunch-hour burst. Backlog clears faster and we’re no longer hitting client timeouts. Please keep us posted if you plan to change defaults again; we rely on burst capacity.

2026-02-20 09:10 (Sofia Ivanova): Full rollout complete for Northbridge Support dedicated cluster. Monitoring for 48h. Follow-up: document this as a known bursty-shape sensitivity in scheduler metrics runbook and ensure baseline suite includes this burst ramp with mixed prompt lengths as a gating shape for scheduler changes.
resolution: Resolved by deploying scheduler fairness + batching adjustments that prevent prefill-heavy admission from fragmenting decode batches under bursty, mixed prompt-length traffic. Validated via internal benchmark replay + canary on customer dedicated cluster; customer confirmed throughput recovery and improved drain time. Follow-ups captured: ensure bursty mixed-length shape is included in baseline gating and keep scheduler flags documented for Dedicated rollouts.
